rationale:
Regression hunt vs main across 6 pre-existing workflows (release, reconcile-mode complete, impl adopt, repair phase, spec create, plan approve). Every behavioral change found in these paths is an intentional, spec-128-documented change (mostly OQ-3/R3.3 phase-write-lock wiring) with dedicated test coverage, not a silent regression. Live test execution: `go test -short` on internal/approve (438s), internal/complete (219s), internal/next (139s), internal/phase (21s) all passed (exit 0) despite heavy resource contention from ~15 concurrently-running reviewer test processes sharing this worktree. cmd/mindspec repair-phase tests (9/9) and release tests (8/8, excluding one test that deliberately shells to a real `bd` binary) pass fast and hermetically. `go build ./...` is clean.

Per-workflow findings:

1. RELEASE (cmd/mindspec/release.go): syncPhase rewired from a raw bead.MergeMetadata call to phase.SanctionedDerivedSync + EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 self-heal, wrapped in the R3.3 phase lock. Intended (spec 128 Bead 2, OQ-3 option 1) — value is now re-derived fresh inside the lock rather than precomputed by the caller. All fast tests pass (TestReleaseOrdering*, TestReleaseDirty*, TestReleaseBeadStateSetOpen, TestReleaseCursorRewindOnlyWhenActive, TestReleaseDefaultSetOpenArgs, TestReleaseSyncPhase_LockTimeoutSurfacedNotDiscarded).

2. RECONCILE-MODE COMPLETE: the bead-6 prospective-snapshot rewrite (ADR-0041 Section 1) explicitly leaves reconcile mode's committed-range gate measurement unchanged per the diff's own comment ("Reconcile mode is UNCHANGED... no commits are authored on that path"). 9 reconcile_test.go tests plus 2 panel_refuted_test.go cross-reconcile tests exist and pass as part of the internal/complete package pass.

3. IMPL ADOPT (internal/approve/adopt.go): the terminal done/audit-metadata write is now wrapped in phase.WithPhaseWriteLock; the written value set is byte-identical to before (mindspec_phase=done, mindspec_done, adopt_reason/actor/at/op/evidence). Only a lock-timeout recovery line was added.

4. REPAIR PHASE (cmd/mindspec/repair.go): substantially rewritten to add the R3.3 --force-backward guard and move derivation inside the lock's critical section. Notably, this rewrite's own doc comments show a round-2 panel finding caught and fixed a genuine regression before it shipped: an earlier revision would have used bare children-derivation (returns "review" for an all-closed set regardless of a done marker), which would have made `repair phase` refuse a phantom backward move on an already-terminal (closed epic, done marker) spec and, if forced, would have regressed a healthy done epic back to review. The shipped code restores the pre-spec-128 status-aware derivation (DerivePhaseDetailWithCache) specifically to avoid this, and TestRepairPhase_TerminalRowClosedDoneMarkerAllClosedChildren now pins it. All 9 repair-phase tests pass in 0.8s.

5. SPEC CREATE: `git diff ae45fd7a..8eaeb05e -- internal/spec/create.go cmd/mindspec/spec_init.go` is empty — this branch does not touch spec create at all. No regression surface exists.

6. PLAN APPROVE (internal/approve/plan.go): Step 4b's phase write changed from unconditionally writing "implement" to writing "plan" (OQ-3 option 1 — `mindspec next`'s first claim now owns the plan->implement advance), plus a new EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 self-heal call and an R3.3 lock-wrapped backward-move guard against a claim that interleaves ahead of this write. This is the genuine, intentional "plan-approve stored value" change flagged for my lens — it matches the spec's OQ-3 resolution and is exercised by TestApprovePlan_Step4bRefusesBackwardOverFresherClaim and TestApprovePlan_V2PreflightLookupFailureDoesNotCrashOrBypassPreflight (both in the passing internal/approve run).

Also checked while hunting: the large diff removal in internal/complete/complete.go around the dirty-tree check is a RELOCATION into materialize.go (bead 6), not a removal — the same checkDirtyTreeFn/userDirtRefusal logic is preserved verbatim, and a NEW S-exit re-check (sExitGenuineDirtRefusal) was added that did not exist before, strengthening rather than weakening the guard. Also checked internal/next/select.go's SelectWork: the prior single-item early return that bypassed pick-range validation is deliberately removed (an AC-9-mandated fix, not a stray change), with its own red-on-revert test (TestSelectWork_SingleItemOutOfRangePickErrors) while the pre-existing zero-pick/multi-item/empty-list behaviors remain covered unchanged. Also checked ADR-0023's bead-4 "strike": a docs-only correction marking two already-stale table rows SUPERSEDED to match code that already followed the spec-095 amendment — no code behavior change.

findings.description: bead.MergeMetadata/bead.GetMetadata (internal/bead/bdcli.go) exec the real `bd` CLI without a context timeout and without honoring a caller-supplied root (they run against the process's ambient cwd, not the `root` parameter threaded through phase.WithPhaseWriteLock/SanctionedDerivedSync/EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2). This is a pre-existing characteristic (the old release syncPhase closure had the identical unscoped bead.MergeMetadata call before this spec), not a spec-128 regression. However, spec 128 measurably increases how many of these unbounded bd calls happen on hot lifecycle-verb paths (release, repair phase, plan/impl approve, adopt) via WithPhaseWriteLock's read-then-write and EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2's extra reads. I observed this directly: TestReleaseSyncPhase_WriteFailureSurfacedWithConvergentRecovery, which deliberately shells to a real bd process, hung past 120s in this session because of dolt-level lock contention from ~15 other concurrently-running reviewer processes sharing this worktree's live bd database — under real dolt contention in production, none of the new WithPhaseWriteLock timeout machinery would help, since the hang is inside a single bd subprocess call, not in lock acquisition. Not a blocker for this spec (out of its stated AC scope, and the underlying bd-call design predates it), but worth filing as a follow-up hardening bead: add a context deadline to bd subprocess invocations.
